A button follows a nearby pointer and settles back on release.

Measure the pointer relative to the button center. Clamp translation to 8px and ease back to zero when the pointer leaves. Keep the hit area fixed, use transform only on an inner surface, and preserve a visible keyboard focus ring.
Do not move the actual hit target. Touch and reduced-motion users get a stationary button.
A toggle knob stretches during a change of state, then returns to a circle.

Use a real checkbox with an associated label. Move its visual thumb between two endpoints over 220ms, stretching the leading edge briefly with scaleX before settling. Keep checked state and assistive-technology state synchronized.
The label and checked state must remain understandable without animation.
A compact navigation panel reveals its items in a short cascade.

Open an accessible navigation disclosure. Reveal items using opacity and a 10px vertical translation, with 35ms between items and a total sequence under 350ms. Reverse the group as one unit on close; restore focus to the trigger.
Hidden links must not remain in the tab order. Do not stagger keyboard focus.
An underline travels between tabs without rebuilding the whole tab row.

Implement the ARIA tabs keyboard pattern. Measure the selected tab and animate one absolutely positioned underline to its left offset and width over 180ms. Update measurements after resize or font loading, and keep panel content stable during the transition.
Selection must still work when animation is disabled and when labels wrap.
Notifications enter from one edge and make room for the next message.

Use one polite live region for status announcements. Enter each toast with 16px translation and opacity over 180ms, then shift existing toasts to make space. Include a dismiss button, pause expiration on hover or focus, and cap visible messages at three.
Urgent errors need a persistent inline home; a timed toast alone is insufficient.
A changing digit flips across a horizontal hinge like a station display.

Split each visual digit into clipped top and bottom halves. Rotate the outgoing upper half to 90 degrees, then rotate the incoming lower half into place over a combined 360ms. Expose one static accessible number and hide decorative digit layers from screen readers.
Keep the final number legible without perspective support. Avoid repeating announcements per frame.
An answer panel opens smoothly while its heading stays in place.

Use a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. Animate a grid row from 0fr to 1fr over 200ms with overflow hidden on the inner wrapper. Fade in the answer slightly after expansion begins. Keep focus on the heading button.
Collapsed content must be inert or unmounted so it cannot receive focus.
A search dialog appears with a small scale change and a steady input.

Use a native dialog opened with showModal. Animate its surface from scale .98 and opacity zero to its final state in 140ms. Focus the search input, support Escape, and restore the opening control on close. Keep results updates separate from the entrance animation.
Never animate the entire document or hide focus behind the dialog.
A card follows a drag directly and springs to the nearest resting slot.

Capture the pointer on drag start and make the card follow the pointer without easing. On release, choose the closest of three slots and settle with a damped spring. Provide left and right buttons as keyboard alternatives and respect pointercancel.
Do not block vertical page scrolling before the user clearly starts a horizontal drag.
A circular progress indicator advances to a measured value.

Draw a circle with a known circumference and animate its stroke-dashoffset to reflect real completed work. Use round caps, a fixed start angle, and an accessible progressbar value. If total work is unknown, use an indeterminate label instead of fabricating a percentage.
Progress must reflect supplied data. Never use a fake loading loop for completed work.
A soft highlight follows the pointer across a group of cards.

Track pointer coordinates in CSS custom properties on the container using requestAnimationFrame. Reveal a clipped radial highlight inside each hovered card while keeping text contrast unchanged. Provide an equivalent fixed border treatment on focus-visible.
Disable pointer tracking for coarse pointers and reduced-motion preferences.
A loading placeholder gives way to content without shifting the page.

Reserve the final content dimensions in the loading skeleton. On actual data resolution, crossfade the placeholder and content over 160ms while retaining the same box. Mark the region aria-busy during loading and provide retry content on failure.
A skeleton must stop when loading fails. Avoid indefinite shimmer or artificial delays.
A submit button changes to a check after a confirmed successful action.

Keep the button width fixed through idle, pending, success, and failure states. After the operation succeeds, draw an SVG check with stroke-dashoffset over 180ms and update the label. Re-enable a clear retry action on failure and announce the status once.
Only show success after the actual action succeeds; preserve useful error details.
Letters arrive on a beat, hold long enough to read, and leave as a single word.

Build a six-second, 16:9 title film. Place large type on a plain field, stagger characters by 60ms with a 24px rise and opacity, hold the assembled word for two seconds, then move it out as one group. Compute every position from time through seek(t).
Use a user-provided wordmark and licensed font. No music is required.
Three product features appear in a short launch sequence with a clear final frame.

Build a twelve-second product film with a two-second title, three two-second feature beats, a two-second benefit summary, and a two-second closing frame. Use user-supplied screenshots or labeled neutral UI diagrams. Carry one shape between scenes using matched positions and size changes.
Do not invent product features, testimonials, or customer logos. Screenshots must be supplied or cleared.
A single supplied metric counts to its final value and holds beside its label.

Build a six-second metric scene. Introduce the label, count from zero to the supplied value over 1.6 seconds using cubic ease-out, then hold the complete value with units and a source caption. Use fixed-width numerals and derive each frame from time.
Use real supplied data and source text. Do not imply measured business results with demo numbers.
A flat device frame enters while its product screen stays readable.

Build an eight-second product screen scene. Slide a simple unbranded device outline upward by 60px with a small tilt correction, hold a user-provided screen inside it, then introduce one concise annotation. Keep the screen region at least half the frame height and avoid a fast camera move.
Use an unbranded outline unless branded assets are cleared. Long screens need a deliberate crop.
Two clearly labeled states share the screen before one expands to fill it.

Build a ten-second comparison with two equally sized panels and explicit labels. Hold the comparison for four seconds, move a divider to emphasize the selected state, then expand that state using a continuous crop. Keep labels outside the moving mask until the expansion completes.
Avoid fabricated before-and-after claims; supplied examples need equivalent scale and framing.
A supplied line mark draws itself before its name fades into view.

Build a five-second SVG logo reveal using a user-supplied simple path. Measure total path length, animate stroke-dashoffset from full length to zero over two seconds, then reveal the name with opacity. End on a static, high-contrast lockup with adequate clear space.
Filled or complex marks may need separate paths. Do not redraw an unlicensed trademark.
A short sentence types on with a quiet caret and an unhurried hold.

Build a seven-second title using a supplied sentence of at most 60 characters. Reveal characters by grapheme cluster at a controlled pace, add a subtle caret, then hold the complete sentence for at least two seconds. Pre-measure the final layout so wrapping does not jump during typing.
Avoid infinite blinking. Do not reveal emoji by UTF-16 code unit.
A circle in one scene becomes the focal object in the next.

Build two four-second scenes connected by one circular shape. End the first scene with the circle at the second scene's target position and size. Interpolate position, scale, and color continuously through a one-second bridge, revealing the new scene inside its mask.
A match cut needs matching geometry; do not disguise an unrelated hard cut with a flash.
A short quotation appears line by line with its attribution in the same frame.

Build a ten-second quotation scene. Break a supplied quote into balanced lines, reveal lines with 120ms spacing, and place the author's name and source below. Hold all text together for at least five seconds before fading the scene.
Never invent a quotation or endorsement. Keep source attribution legible in the final output.
A schematic product separates into labeled layers and returns to its assembled state.

Build a twelve-second schematic with three to five user-defined product layers. Start assembled, separate layers along one shared axis, reveal labels outside the object silhouette, hold, then reassemble in reverse order. Use simple geometry when no cleared model is supplied.
Label a schematic as illustrative; do not imply hidden engineering details are verified.
A portrait product film moves through a problem, a useful action, and a closing card.

Build a fifteen-second 9:16 film with three five-second beats: a supplied problem, a product action that addresses it, and a closing card. Keep essential text in the central safe region, limit each card to twelve words, and use one directional transition throughout.
Leave room for platform controls and captions. Use only supplied or cleared product claims.
Three large numerals mark time before a launch title appears.

Build a five-second countdown with the digits three, two, and one each occupying one second. Scale each numeral from .92 to 1 with a short opacity reveal, then replace the final numeral with a supplied title for two seconds. Use time-derived states and avoid strobing.
If used for a real event, keep displayed timing synchronized to the actual event clock.
Three labeled steps connect in sequence as a dot travels between them.

Build an eight-second process diagram with three supplied step labels. Reveal nodes one at a time, draw each connector after its source node settles, and move one dot along the completed path. Hold the complete diagram for two seconds with all labels visible.
The moving dot is illustrative unless it is driven by actual process data.
A small ranked chart animates between two supplied snapshots of data.

Build an eight-second horizontal bar chart for four supplied categories. Interpolate numeric values between two snapshots, sort rows at each frame, and ease each row toward its current rank. Keep labels and values outside the bars and use a shared fixed axis.
Show units, dates, and source. Never change the axis scale silently to exaggerate differences.
A data line draws across a stable axis and ends with a labeled value.

Build a six-second line chart using supplied dated observations. Render axes and units first, then reveal the data path with a left-to-right clip over two seconds. Add the final value and source caption after the reveal; hold the final chart for three seconds.
Preserve chronological spacing and label any missing observations.
A ring fills segment by segment and connects each share to a label.

Build a seven-second donut chart from positive supplied values. Compute each segment's fraction from the total, reveal the arcs in sequence, then introduce directly associated labels and a total in the center. Keep percentage precision consistent.
Reject zero totals and negative values. Do not rely on color alone to identify segments.
A line connects dated milestones while each caption has time to be read.

Build a twelve-second timeline with four supplied dates and captions. Draw a horizontal rail, introduce each marker in chronological order at equal temporal beats, and reveal its caption nearby. End on the full timeline with a three-second hold.
Distinguish proposed roadmap dates from completed events.
A packet follows a highlighted route through a small network diagram.

Build a ten-second diagram with six nodes and a single supplied route. Draw the full graph faintly, highlight the route's edges, and move a dot through them at constant distance-per-second speed. Pause briefly at the destination and show its label.
Label the topology as illustrative unless it represents a real documented network.
An application stack separates into interface, service, and storage layers.

Build a nine-second isometric stack with three labeled plates. Start with the stack assembled, lift each plate along the same vertical axis, reveal interface, service, and storage captions, and use a subtle connector to show the request path.
Use the project's actual components when supplied; generic layers must be labeled as a schematic.
A supplied series of stage counts narrows into a labeled conversion funnel.

Build an eight-second funnel with four supplied stage counts. Size stages relative to the first value, introduce them from top to bottom, then display the percentage moving between adjacent stages. Keep the full counts and stage definitions visible.
Reject negative counts and disclose if stages overlap rather than represent a strict funnel.
A short equation forms term by term, with each variable explained nearby.

Build a ten-second equation using a supplied expression with at most five terms. Allocate positions from the final layout, reveal each term in reading order, and attach a short plain-language definition beneath it. Hold the whole equation without moving its baseline.
Do not invent a mathematical derivation. Use plain text or user-supplied typeset assets.
A four-step process loops once around a circle before stopping on the complete diagram.

Build a ten-second circular process diagram with four labeled nodes. Reveal nodes in order, connect them with directional arcs, and move a single marker through one complete cycle. Stop movement after the cycle and hold the labeled diagram.
Keep the reading order clear and provide a linear text equivalent.
Three points move on tilted orbits around a central body.

Build a looping twelve-second orbital scene with Canvas 2D projection. Compute three circular paths in 3D, rotate their planes, project them with a fixed perspective, and sort bodies by depth before drawing. Use a restrained trail and an unchanging central body.
This is a stylized orbital illustration, not a physically accurate simulation.
A wire cube turns around two axes with a fixed camera.

Build a twelve-second loop by rotating a cube's eight vertices around the Y axis and gently tilting around X. Project the vertices with a fixed perspective and draw the twelve edges with depth-aware opacity. Match the loop endpoints exactly.
Do not call perspective projection isometric unless parallel lines are actually preserved.
Soft green ribbons drift across a dark field without external textures.

Build a twelve-second Canvas background using several translucent ribbons. Compute ribbon height from a sum of slow sine waves, add smaller frequency detail, and layer strokes with decreasing opacity. Use periodic time functions so the first and last frame match.
This Canvas study approximates light curtains. Keep contrast sufficient for any overlaid content.
A field of points gathers into a word or a simple supplied silhouette.

Build a twelve-second Canvas scene with a seeded field of 400 points. Sample target positions from a short word rendered to an offscreen canvas, assign each point a stable target, and interpolate from scattered positions to the silhouette with staggered timing. Hold the assembled form before returning.
Use a supplied font and word. Avoid randomizing targets each frame or exceeding the point budget on mobile.
A wireframe landscape moves under a fixed low camera.

Build a Three.js plane with modest subdivisions and displace its vertices using smooth procedural noise. Advance the sampled noise coordinates over time, keep the camera fixed, and color the wireframe with one accent on a dark background. Dispose of geometry and materials on teardown.
Cap device pixel ratio at 1.5 and reduce subdivisions on mobile. Provide a static fallback.
A transparent geometric object turns slowly above a matte surface.

Build a Three.js scene with one beveled or rounded geometric object, a matte plane, and two large area-like lights. Use a physical transmission material with restrained roughness and a procedural or cleared environment. Rotate the object slowly while keeping the camera still.
Transmission can be expensive. Provide an opaque fallback and avoid requiring an external HDR map.
A narrow ribbon follows a curved path through a quiet scene.

Build a Three.js ribbon mesh along a closed Catmull-Rom curve. Sample a stable frame along the curve, move a highlight along its length using a shader uniform, and use a soft directional light to make its twists readable. Keep the mesh topology fixed.
Avoid rebuilding geometry on every frame; cap the path segment count.
Three flat product panels drift at different depths with a small camera tilt.

Build a CSS perspective scene with three supplied product panels. Give each a fixed translateZ depth and a slow, low-amplitude vertical oscillation with different phases. Limit pointer-driven camera tilt to four degrees and keep panel text readable.
Disable tilt on touch devices and provide a flat layout for reduced motion.
Concentric rings rotate at different speeds around a dark central opening.

Build a Three.js scene with six torus meshes sharing one center. Give successive rings smaller radii and slightly different rotation speeds; animate a subtle emissive accent without postprocessing. Keep a fixed camera looking through the opening.
Avoid flashing emission and excessive bloom. Dispose all meshes and stop the frame loop when hidden.
A mesh rises into crossing waves under a fixed light.

Build a moderately subdivided Three.js plane with vertex-shader displacement from two crossing sine waves. Recompute or approximate the normal consistently with displacement, light the surface from one direction, and use a quiet solid material. Drive wave phase from elapsed time.
This is a stylized wave study. Real water needs additional optical and simulation work.
A small cluster of reflective spheres moves through a slow repeating pattern.

Build a Three.js study with five metallic spheres of different radii following periodic paths. Use large light panels or a cleared environment for readable reflections, and keep roughness above zero. Maintain separation unless an actual signed-distance blending shader is implemented.
Separate spheres are not fluid simulation. Label the preview as a material and motion study.
A sparse starfield drifts past a fixed camera with a slow sense of depth.

Build a Canvas scene with 300 seeded stars at stable 3D coordinates. Move the camera forward slowly, project points with perspective, and recycle stars beyond the near plane. Keep point size and brightness bounded, and leave a dark region for content.
Avoid full-screen flashes or high-speed optical flow; offer a static starfield for reduced motion.
Points on a sphere turn together while the rear hemisphere stays faint.

Distribute 500 points on a sphere with a Fibonacci lattice, rotate them around the vertical axis, and project them to a Canvas. Draw the far hemisphere first with lower opacity, then the front hemisphere. Use a twelve-second rotation period and one fixed light cue.
A point sphere does not represent geographic data. Supply a cleared map mask if continents are needed.
Nested organic contours breathe slowly around an off-center focal point.

Build a Canvas background with twenty nested closed contours sampled at 120 angles each. Modulate each radius with low-frequency periodic waves, vary line opacity by ring, and animate the phase slowly. Keep stroke thickness stable across resolution changes.
Limit contour contrast behind text and stop drawing when the scene leaves the viewport.
Repeated rectangular frames create a slow journey through a tunnel.

Build a Canvas scene with sixteen rectangular frames at evenly spaced depths. Move them toward the camera at a constant speed, wrap their depth deterministically, and fade the closest and farthest frames. Apply only a small periodic rotation to the complete tunnel.
Keep travel slow and provide a still frame for reduced-motion users.
